Maybe break up para 2, as it is quite long. And connect with a broader and longer history of individual diffs (or differential psychology) in general. We discussed this in our last meeting. ### Discussion

I think the general structure works. But of course, we need a little more flow to make it easier to read. 

I would do a few things here. 

1. Be disciplined in word count for the discussion, as this will make you select carefully which paragraphs are required and which can be relegated to a sentence or just removed. 
2. Decide on themes to cover as that will help you organise paragraphs. e.g., opening para - main contribution. Then theoretical advance etc. in the next paras, then limitations, future directions. 
3. As per the feedback for the intro, early on in the discussion, I would connect back to the broader theme of linking together experimental, differential and computational approaches to understand the cognitive processes that underpin face perception. Maybe even in the first para we could say this study shows how knowledge or novel insight can be gained from linking together blah blah and blah approaches. So we would be concluding something about the value of the method for the field, as well as the specific results.
4. I would read the following Phillips and White paper and cite it. Maybe you meant to cite this already, but I could not see it. https://bpspsychub.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/bjop.12794
It is more about deep learning models, but there are many links nonetheless. I am sure it will help you think about the value of estimating latent variables and such like.
